# scamp_kubernetes_cluster (Resource)

Manages a Kubernetes cluster: a control plane run by ServersCamp, free, and node pools of servers in your private network. The API has its own name under the cluster domain with a certificate we renew. Nodes have no public address; services reach the internet through a load balancer.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "scamp_kubernetes_cluster" "prod" {
  name = "prod"

  node_pool = [
    {
      name       = "workers"
      plan       = "basic-4g"
      node_count = 3
    },
    {
      name       = "fast"
      plan       = "hf-8g"
      node_count = 1
      labels     = { tier = "fast" }
    },
  ]
}

resource "local_sensitive_file" "kubeconfig" {
  content  = scamp_kubernetes_cluster.prod.kubeconfig
  filename = "${path.module}/prod-kubeconfig.yaml"
}

output "api_url" {
  value = scamp_kubernetes_cluster.prod.api_url
}
```

`terraform apply` returns once the cluster runs and every node is ready, usually in a few minutes.

## Changing node pools

A pool grows, shrinks and changes `max_pods` and `labels` in place. Shrinking drains the newest nodes and
deletes them. A pool keeps its plan: to move nodes to another plan, add a pool under a new name with that
plan and remove the old pool in the same apply. The new pool is added first, so the cluster always has one.

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the cluster: 3 to 32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. It is the start of the API address. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `node_pool` (Attributes List) Node pools, 1 to 5. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pool))

### Optional

- `network_id` (String) UUID of the network, attached to a router. Without it the account's default network. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `storage_box_id` (String) UUID of a Storage Box on the same router, shared by the pods as a ReadWriteMany storage class. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `version` (String) Kubernetes version, e.g. 1.36. Without it the default version. Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Read-Only

- `api_private_url` (String) Address of the Kubernetes API in the private network.
- `api_url` (String) https:// address of the Kubernetes API.
- `hostname` (String) The API's name.
- `id` (String) The cluster's id.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) An admin kubeconfig, made once when the cluster is ready, with a client certificate for a year.
- `state` (String) active once the cluster runs, failed or deleting; anything else while it is being made.

<a id="nestedatt--node_pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_pool`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the pool, same rule as the cluster name. Nodes are named after it.
- `node_count` (Number) Number of nodes, 1 or more.
- `plan` (String) Server plan of every node, e.g. basic-4g. 2 GB of memory or more.

Optional:

- `labels` (Map of String) Node labels, on every node of the pool. Pods already placed stay where they are.
- `max_pods` (Number) Pods a node takes, 8 to 250. Without it by the node's memory: 16 a GB, 110 at most. A change restarts the kubelet of the nodes; running pods stay.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import scamp_kubernetes_cluster.prod 4e5b1e18-9802-4d1a-962b-d03a32f5b5d5
```

The kubeconfig is made on the first read after the import.
